analyst_view.overall: Early view: a game between two teams level on 9 points around the top-eight line. Club Brugge (9th) won 2-1 at PSV on matchday 4, while Liverpool (8th) lost 3-2 at Fenerbahce after poor set-piece defending, then lost 1-0 at home to Arsenal before winning 3-1 at Crystal Palace. Andoni Iraola's side are still finding their feet; Ryan Gravenberch missed the Fenerbahce game with a heel injury.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals. Liverpool's games are rarely tight, with five goals in Istanbul and four at Palace, and their attack (Bradley Barcola, Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz) has started to click. Brugge score at home and Liverpool's set-piece defending has been described as cheap and messy, so I stay with a lively game.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and I stay with it. Liverpool should have more of the ball, but Brugge are dangerous on the counter through Carlos Forbs and in the air through Nicolo Tresoldi. Nothing I found moves the figure.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards and I lean slightly higher. Brugge had three players booked at PSV, and Liverpool's recent games have been heated, with Alexis Mac Allister booked in Istanbul and accused of trying to provoke Noni Madueke at Anfield. A game with top-eight places at stake should be more tense than the estimate suggests.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.5 shots, which looks high. Liverpool's expensive forward line has scored fewer league goals than Ipswich this season, and Brugge were compact enough to win at PSV. I expect a total around 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.5 shots on target and I lean slightly lower. Liverpool's attack is improving, but it has not been efficient this season, and Brugge allowed PSV only one goal in Eindhoven. I expect a total closer to ten.
